title: Levenda's archival assessment of MJ-12 and his talk with Stanton Friedman
place_text: National Archives / Library of Congress; Contact in the Desert

tellings.quote: Those documents to me look real.

plain: The author Peter Levenda says the MJ-12 papers, a disputed set of documents describing a secret committee of twelve officials called Majestic 12 said to handle UFO matters, look genuine to him. He tells Michels he weighed them against records he knew from the National Archives and the Library of Congress, and talked them over with Stanton Friedman, a UFO researcher who championed the papers, at a UFO conference called Contact in the Desert. "Those documents to me look real," Levenda says, which if right would mean a secret government UFO panel existed in the 1940s and 50s.
